items.title: 63477_Joe Darensbourg oral history interview
items.q: But he mostly taught theory and harmony, and stuff that I shouldn't have been in, that's what I'm saying, but that damn Papa Mutt talked me into going there.

ctx.x: And I've heard it described as a laser-beam that would cut through metal. I think you either liked his tone or didn't like his tone, you know. I personally like Mutt's playing a whole lot. But many musicians have said the same thing that you do, Mutt was the weakest one in the band.

As a matter of fact, they had a teacher here that taught the musicians that... He was a symphony man. His name was Doc Heiner. [SPELLS] He had his kind of school of music in Pasadena. I don't know why I went there in the first place, but Mutt was the cause of it.
Oh, you went there when you were out here in the Twenties, the late Twenties.
